Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "path": "memory/continual-arc-task-fd411bef.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC task-fd411bef — separator signal from hollow 3 marker

Verified solution: test submission accepted (0 wrong attempts; 2 demo requests).

## Observed rule

The scene has repeated straight parallel separator lines of color 2 and one or more hollow 3 markers: a 3x3 ring of 3s with a 2 at its center. Each marker is centered on one of the separator lines. It emits a color-1 signal perpendicular to the separator orientation, along the marker's center row/column, spanning the whole grid. On the signal row/column, zero cells become 1, but existing marker cells and separator intersections (2s) stay as-is. When the signal reaches every other parallel separator, it creates a 3-cell-wide perpendicular halo around that crossing: the neighboring cells on both sides of the crossing become 1, including separator-line cells in those adjacent rows/columns. The center crossing cell remains 2. Preserve all original 3-marker cells and other cells.

Equivalently: vertical 2 separators + marker centered on one => fill its entire horizontal center row with 1 except marker and separator crossings; for each other vertical separator, color the three cells centered on the crossing in the two adjacent rows as 1 while leaving the crossing itself 2. Horizontal separators work by rotation (full vertical center column and 3-wide halo at other horizontal lines). Multiple markers independently emit signals; output patterns may overlap.

## Demonstrations

- Demo 1: 10x10, horizontal 2 lines at rows 1 and 6, hollow 3 marker centered at (row 1, col 5). Output colors the full vertical centerline col 5 with 1 except the source marker and horizontal-line crossing; around row 6, it colors the neighboring rows' cells at cols 4–6 and row 6 cols 4 and 6, preserving the crossing at (6,5)=2.
- Demo 2: 15x12, vertical 2 lines at cols 3 and 9; markers centered at (2,3) and (11,9). Each colors its entire center row with 1 except markers/separator intersections; halos color cols 8–10 on rows 1 and 3 around crossing (2,9), and cols 2–4 on rows 10 and 12 around (11,3). The crossing centers remain 2.
- Test: 16x18, vertical 2 lines at cols 2,7,11,16; markers centered at (2,2) and (12,11). Their rows are filled with 1s except marker/2 crossings; halos form at the other separator columns on adjacent rows. Accepted.

## Fast solving checklist

1. Identify orientation and coordinates of the 2 separator lines and each hollow 3x3 marker centered on a separator.
2. For each marker, color its whole center row (vertical separators) or center column (horizontal separators) with 1, preserving original marker cells and separator intersections.
3. At each other parallel separator, color the 3-cell-wide perpendicular neighborhood around the signal crossing; leave the center intersection as 2.
4. Verify dimensions and retain all untouched cells.
"
